replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics has always been a big part of my life. I enjoy solving problems and seeing how different concepts fit together. I’ve always liked the logical structure of math, and it feels satisfying when I understand something completely. I’ve done well in it and find it useful in computer science.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I do get a bit anxious sometimes, especially with more complex problems. My parents were both in STEM, so I’ve been used to a lot of pressure, but I’ve worked on managing it.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used AI to help with math problems. I’d type in a question and it would break it down, showing me the steps. replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a. Plug the values of a, b, and c into the formula. Calculate the discriminant to see if you'll get real or complex roots. Then simplify and solve for x.

Start with the derivative, f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Plug them back into the original function to find the y-values. Then, examine the second derivative to classify each point as a local maximum, minimum, or point of inflection.
